lead: Atlanta's tree-covered neighborhoods, older bungalows and fast-growing apartment market shape its fire damage. SootMend helps homes and businesses across the city recover from fire, smoke and soot.
risk: kitchen and electrical fires, apartment fires, and space heater fires during cold snaps
why: Atlanta neighborhoods such as Kirkwood, Grant Park, West End and Virginia-Highland have many early 1900s bungalows and craftsman homes with older wiring and crawl spaces. Most homes heat with electricity, and space heaters come out when winter cold snaps hit.

More than half of Atlanta households rent, and large apartment buildings have gone up across Midtown, Buckhead and along the BeltLine. Fires in these buildings spread smoke through halls and shared ventilation. Atlanta's humid climate also means soot and smoke residue stain quickly if cleanup is delayed.
problems: Apartment fires and smoke in nearby units
Midtown, Buckhead and along the BeltLine
Kirkwood, Grant Park and West End
tips: Turn off space heaters when you leave the room or go to sleep.
Have older homes' wiring checked by a licensed electrician.
Keep a lid nearby to smother pan fires.
Know your building's exits and alarm locations.
insurance: Georgia homeowners and renters should keep a written log of every call with their adjuster and ask for a copy of the estimate before repairs begin.
areas: SootMend works across Atlanta, including Midtown, Buckhead, Virginia-Highland, Inman Park, Kirkwood, Grant Park, West End and East Atlanta.

faq.q: Can smoke from a neighbor's apartment fire damage my unit in Atlanta?
faq.a: Yes. Smoke moves through halls, shared vents and wall gaps. Even without flames, you may need cleaning and odor removal. Report it to your landlord and your renters insurer.
